$comment: The KernelSU late-load build this target would pair with. Written ahead of
the build that proves it: quest3 is not in src/targets.json, so nothing
reads this file yet -- generate_feed.py only sees a target the feed knows
about. It is here because these are properties of the target rather than
of whoever builds it, and because two of them are not guesses.
MEASURED on the device (5.10.240-g55be3759aea4, build 52345320035400520):
CONFIG_MODULES=y, CONFIG_MODULE_UNLOAD=y and CONFIG_MODULE_SIG is NOT
set -- an unsigned module is loadable. CONFIG_MODVERSIONS=y, which the
build already answers by emptying Module.symvers so __versions comes out
zero-length and ksud resolves the undefined symbols from /proc/kallsyms
before init_module; that is how every target here loads, not something
particular to this one.
A late-load driven from an adb shell reaches init_module on this device.
Tried with the android14-6.1 module from another target, deliberately, to
find out where it would stop: vermagic and the version check both passed
and it failed on symbol names alone --
kernelsu: no symbol version for module_layout
kernelsu: Unknown symbol _printk (err -2)
kernelsu: Unknown symbol kmalloc_trace (err -2)
kernelsu: Unknown symbol __alloc_pages (err -2)
... 10 in total
all of which are the 6.x spellings of things 5.10 calls something else
(printk, kmem_cache_alloc_trace, __alloc_pages_nodemask). So the gate is
a module built for the right series, and nothing further down.
NOT MEASURED -- 'kmi' below is the one value here that is a judgement.
Quest 3 shipped on a 5.10 Qualcomm BSP of the android12 era, which is why
it says android12-5.10, but android13-5.10 is the same kernel version and
ddk-min publishes both. Deciding it needs no device:
1. build this entry (the kernelsu-extra job, or the same action by hand)
2. python3 src/kernelsu/tools/extract_target_symvers.py <vmlinux> syms
-- a vmlinux recovered from the running kernel does answer here; the
one this target was derived from yields 14056 exact CRCs
3. python3 src/kernelsu/tools/audit_module_against_target.py \
kernelsu-quest3.ko <vmlinux> syms
MISSING_SYMBOL is the fatal class -- a name the kernel does not have at
all, which is what the 6.1 module failed on and what kallsyms resolution
cannot rescue. MISSING_EXPORT is not: those are resolved from kallsyms.
The KMI whose module audits with an empty MISSING_SYMBOL list is the right
one. The tool is trustworthy here: run against the android14-6.1 module it
named exactly the ten symbols the device's own dmesg did.
'id' is quest3 rather than a shared one: no other target loads this module.
'patchSets' is empty -- this device has no vendor hardening the sets exist
for -- and 'config' goes with a set, so it is empty too.
